newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - Sept 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - Sept 24.

text.p: - Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
-- NURSES SEEK JUMP IN PAY AND END TO LOCAL BARGAINING

Representatives of 500,000 nurses, midwives and health visitors have called for an end to local pay bargaining and a 'substantial' national pay increase. The call is at odds with government guidelines for public sector pay increases. The calls follow a deal in February in which a national pay increase of 2 percent was to be supplemented by local pay offers from NHS Trusts. Seven months on, over one third of Trusts have yet to make a local pay offer.
-- CITY WORRIES OVER EMU UNFOUNDED, REPORT SAYS

A report from a senior City working group has suggested that the City of London will retain its strong position in Europe regardless of whether the UK enters European monetary union (Emu). The only area likely to be significantly affected by Emu is the money markets, because of their close links with the implementation of monetary policy by the future European central bank.
-- TORIES MAY CURB RIGHT OF APPEAL ON UNFAIR DISMISSALS

The launch of the annual report of the government's deregulation task force has been accompanied by suggestions that a future Conservative government may remove the right of appeal against unfair dismissal for future employees in small businesses. The proposal, which would affect more than 90 percent of companies and 15 percent of the workforce, would be put out for consultation by business leaders and other organizations.
-- EU EFFORT TO RESCUE BEEF SECTOR 'BLOCKED'

As European Union farm ministers have been meeting in Ireland to discuss measures to help the beef industry, the British government has been accused of blocking EU efforts by abandoning a deal struck with its EU partners. Agriculture commissioner Franz Fischler claimed that Britain's U-turn on the cull of 125,000 cattle did nothing to restore public confidence in beef after the BSE crisis.
-- FRESH ROW ON GAS PRICE CONTROLS

The on-going battle between British Gas and the industry regulator Ofgas has flared again, this time over controversial price controls for British Gas's pipeline distribution arm TransCo. In a letter to the Financial Times newspaper, British Gas deputy chairman Philip Rogerson accused Ofgas of attempting to influence the Monopolies and Mergers Commission ahead of a possible referral of the issue to that body.
-- VOLKSWAGEN CHIEF HITS AT COMPONENTS INDUSTRY

Volkswagen has claimed that it would like to treble its annual spending on motor components in the UK, to 1.5 billion sterling, within the next three years but it is being frustrated by the quality and productivity of the UK components industry. However, the VW claims are in sharp contrast to praise for the UK industry from VW's German counterparts Mercedes-Benz and BMW, both of whom recently announced components contracts with UK suppliers.
-- TV TRANSMISSION GROUP MUST CURB PRICES UNTIL 2002

National Telecommunications (NTL), the privatized transmission and engineering arm of the former Independent Broadcasting Authority, has been told by the telecommunications watchdog Oftel to reduce by 4 million stg the 57.4 million stg total fees it charges the ITV companies, Channel 4 and S4C for broadcast transmission services. NTL is not to protest against the price curbs.
-- PROFIT WARNING BATTERS SHARES IN BERISFORD

Kitchens and joinery group Berisford saw one third of its stock market value slide on Monday after issuing a warning that industrial action in the UK and problems in the US would hit this year's profits. Some analysts downgraded pre-tax profit forecasts from 34 million stg to 24 million stg for the year. The warning of problems at the group's Welbilt US subsidiary comes just three months after Berisford said the company was doing well.
-- SCHOLL TAKES 29 MILLION STG EXCEPTIONAL

Scholl group, which specialises in foot health products, has reported a pre-tax loss of 21.9 million stg for the six months to June 30, and announced it is taking an exceptional charge of 29.4 million stg for restructuring. The company is to concentrate on the Scholl brand, and will withdraw from a number of other businesses, including herbal remedies company Gerard House.
-- XENOVA 25 MILLION STG TEST FOR BIOTECH MARKET

Slough-based biotechnology company Xenova will announce on Tuesday plans for a 25 million stg London listing to supplement its Nasdaq quotation in the US. The offering, designed to raise cash to help Xenova take its experimental drugs to the next stage of development, will test the subdued biotech listing market. Xenova extracts medicines from natural sources such as plants, fungi and bacteria, with the main focus of its products being cancer.
